title: Secure cluster access in 4 steps
subtitle: From zero to a production-ready Kubernetes authentication webhook — backed by the identity provider you already trust.

steps.title: Install Guard
steps.description: Deploy the Guard webhook server into any Kubernetes cluster — EKS, GKE, AKS, or on-prem — via the CLI installer or Helm.

steps.title: Initialize PKI & Provider
steps.description: Generate a self-signed CA and TLS client certificates bound to your identity provider — GitHub, GitLab, Google, Azure, LDAP, or static tokens.

steps.title: Wire Up the API Server
steps.description: Point your Kubernetes API server's authentication-token-webhook-config-file at the generated kubeconfig so every token review routes through Guard.

steps.title: Authenticate & Enforce RBAC
steps.description: Users log in with their existing provider credentials. Guard maps their identity and groups so your existing Kubernetes RBAC rules just work.
